title: Release changelog extraction treats version headings inside fenced examples as release boundaries
body:
Found at `317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78`, `scripts/create_github_release.py:79-108`, while auditing https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/55. The section scanner treats Markdown headings inside fenced example code as real release boundaries, silently deleting the rest of the notes.

Minimal CHANGELOG.md:

````markdown
## 1.2.3

Example:

```md
## 9.9.9
```

Remaining details.

## 1.2.2
old
````

Expected: the 1.2.3 body contains the whole fenced example and `Remaining details.`. Actual: the body ends at `Example:` and the opening fence, leaving invalid Markdown and dropping real release information. A requested version that appears only inside a fenced example can also select example text as release notes.

Reproduce from the template root (no real publishing):

```sh
python3 -B <<'PY'
import sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from create_github_release import extract_changelog_entry
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / 'CHANGELOG.md'
    path.write_text('## 1.2.3\n\nExample:\n\n```md\n## 9.9.9\n```\n\nRemaining details.\n\n## 1.2.2\nold')
    print(repr(extract_changelog_entry(path, '1.2.3')))
PY
```

The JS and Python snapshot functions were executed offline and both returned the truncated body. The Rust source has the same boundary error in `next_section_re`, which matches `^## [` without fence state; the above CLI reproduction uses a local gh stub. No Rust template build was run on the constrained downstream machine.

Workaround: use indented example code or avoid version-shaped headings inside fenced changelog examples until the scanner is fixed. Do not silently delete the example or the later prose from the actual release.

Suggested fix: find exact release headings only outside Markdown code fences (both backticks and tildes, matching closing delimiter/length), or parse Markdown to an AST and slice by top-level heading offsets. Preserve body bytes/indentation, fail explicitly on missing required entries, and add tests for a fenced next-version heading, a target version only inside a fence, CRLF and multiple change subsections. The downstream PR adds these regressions in `js/tests/ci-github-release.test.js` and fixes its shared release-content helper; the Rust/Python publication programs are template-specific and are not vendored into the product.

title: Missing lychee report is reported as all_archived=true and exit 0
body:
Found during the complete template comparison for https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/44 (issue 43).

## Reproduction

At revision `317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78`, in a fresh checkout with no `lychee/missing-report.md`:

```sh
LYCHEE_OUTPUT=lychee/missing-report.md LYCHEE_EXIT_CODE=2 python3 scripts/check_web_archive.py
```

Expected: nonzero status explaining that the failed checker produced no report. Current missing-file branch explicitly sets `all_archived=true` and exits/returns 0. This can suppress the workflow's final failure condition when lychee crashes, cannot write its report, or the configured paths disagree. The missing-file branch itself is the static reproduction; downloaded template reference code was inspected without executing it.

Source: https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78/scripts/check_web_archive.py#L153

This differs from the previously reported non-HTTP parsing and recovered-link aggregation defects: there is no report to parse at all.

## Workaround

Make the workflow fail on any nonzero lychee exit, independently of `all_archived`; use archive URLs only as repair suggestions. Preserve the report as an artifact with `if-no-files-found: error`.

## Suggested code fix

Treat a missing report as an error (throw or return 1), write `all_archived=false`, and add a subprocess regression test with a nonexistent `LYCHEE_OUTPUT` and a nonzero checker exit. The test must assert a nonzero process exit and no `all_archived=true` output. Handle an unreadable or empty/malformed report after a failed checker the same way.

The downstream PR implements a missing-report regression test and an independent final lychee exit gate. No network or Wayback access is needed to reproduce this branch.

title: Security terminal gate can pass while the separate CodeQL check reports findings
body:
The Security workflow's terminal gate can succeed when CodeQL finds vulnerabilities: github/codeql-action/analyze completes successfully after uploading results, while GitHub publishes findings through a separate Advanced Security check. The terminal gate currently observes only job outcomes. Requiring the aggregate workflow alone therefore does not enforce a clean CodeQL result.

This is an integration gap rather than a failure of the official analyze action. I observed it in https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40675994571 at dfb1f91a842ba3c699699ba94353e7d572e0b65f: all workflow jobs and the terminal gate succeeded, but the separate CodeQL check (122774900583) failed and the complete PR-merge alert API returned ten findings. These are website results, not a claim that the template currently has open vulnerabilities.

The pinned template configuration has the same shape:
https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78/.github/workflows/security.yml

A possible correction is to write analyze's SARIF output to an explicit directory and run a dependency-free result gate afterward. Reject missing/invalid reports, unsuccessful tool invocations, and findings in every run/file, while retaining the normal Code Scanning upload and all queries. This makes the CodeQL job and aggregate workflow accurately fail together. Alternatively, require the independent Code Scanning check explicitly and document that the aggregate workflow is insufficient on its own.

The website implementation in https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/32 tests missing/malformed reports, all severity levels, multiple files/runs and actual CLI exit statuses. It also replays the real downloaded JavaScript SARIF (ten findings, rejected) and a clean Python SARIF (accepted). Its workflow regression fails before the local result gate and passes afterward. GitHub documents analyze's local output directory and sarif-output at https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370/analyze/action.yml.

title: CodeQL emits diff-limit warnings for PRs touching 300 or more files
body:
The CodeQL v4 setup in this template inherits diff-informed analysis. For pull requests touching at least 300 files, its compare API cannot supply the complete file list, so CodeQL emits a warning and falls back to full analysis.

Affected configuration: [security.yml at 317c243](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/blob/317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78/.github/workflows/security.yml#L59) (init at line 59, analyze at line 68; no job-level diff-analysis override).

Observed reproduction using the same v4 configuration: [konard/konard.github.io run 40674729926](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40674729926), head b9e68d463783128440e3a410b543cff3ec61a3a6, PR 32 with 314 changed files. JavaScript, Python and Actions analyses finish successfully but report:

> Cannot retrieve the full diff because there are too many (300) changed files in the pull request.

The additional files are requested research/log evidence, not additional analyzed production source. This is not a claim that an observed run in this template failed; the shared source/configuration demonstrates the same boundary.

The [v4 action source](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370/src/diff-informed-analysis-utils.ts#L157) explicitly warns when the compare result reaches 300 files. Its [feature definition](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370/src/feature-flags.ts#L243) and [test](https://github.com/github/codeql-action/blob/9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370/src/diff-informed-analysis-utils.test.ts#L113) support setting CODEQL_ACTION_DIFF_INFORMED_QUERIES to the string false. The [official incremental-analysis guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/find-and-fix-code-vulnerabilities/scan-from-the-command-line/incremental-analysis) recommends full analysis if a diff source is truncated.

Suggested handling: choose full analysis explicitly for large/evidence-heavy PRs (or all PRs for a small repository) with this environment setting inherited by both init and analyze. Keep every default query and language enabled. A hosted regression with 300+ changed files should complete all analyses without diff-limit warnings; do not suppress the warning or skip security scanning.

The website correction and before/after evidence are tracked in https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/32.

title: Retry transient artifact transport failures without rerunning validated tests
body:
While investigating konard/konard.github.io#31 / https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/pull/32, the main workflow failed after **all browser regressions passed**, solely because artifact creation encountered transient DNS failure:

https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40662150605

At the WebKit evidence upload: `Failed to CreateArtifact: Unable to make request: ENOTFOUND` (09:15:33 UTC on 2026-10-28). This prevented the tested site from building/deploying.

The current template also uses single-attempt artifact upload steps, including Pages publication. GitHub's SDK does retry HTTP 429/5xx internally, but `@actions/artifact` 6.3.1's `artifact-twirp-client` catch explicitly throws `NetworkError` immediately for ENOTFOUND / ECONNRESET / ETIMEDOUT / ECONNREFUSED / EHOSTUNREACH, bypassing that retry loop. Re-running all tests is unnecessary when only the upload failed.

Suggested improvement: wrap artifact operations in a small bounded transport retry (for both diagnostic uploads and release-critical Pages uploads), preserving failure on exhausted retries, missing evidence, or permanent 4xx/auth/quota failures. On a retry, reconcile an artifact that may have finalized before its response was lost, so it cannot cause a duplicate-name conflict. Do not make uploads globally continue-on-error. Test recovery and exhaustion with injected network errors, plus immediate permanent refusal and empty-directory failures.

The website PR contains a reusable implementation and focused regression cases. A local JavaScript action is used so the runner supplies artifact runtime credentials without exposing them to shell steps.

Affected template snapshot: `317c243a7cc832b0abfe4d30989c5095d17fcd78`. Examples: `.github/workflows/docs.yml:74,90`, `links.yml:126`, `release.yml:431,904`.
